rationale.product_understanding: analysis.md separates supplied facts (lines 8-14), seven labelled assumptions including the load-bearing owner-seat reading (line 18) and the Admin settings inference flagged as needing confirmation (line 20), and ten explicit unknowns (lines 26-33); the UI copy follows that declared assumption (implementation/index.html:269).
rationale.ux_reasoning: The path is create -> success -> optional invite (implementation/index.html:56-291) with skip on both steps (implementation/app.js:1091, 1114), a contextual resume card (implementation/app.js:873-912) and a deep-link guard in setView, so a solo owner reaches a project without inviting. The only friction is an invented 2-character minimum (implementation/app.js:315) that rejects a valid one-character name.
rationale.design_judgment: analysis.md §4 gives eight decisions with explicit costs, e.g. invitations being one click less discoverable (line 80), and reasons about moving the role guide below the form on mobile (line 89).
rationale.visual_hierarchy: The desktop crops show one clear primary action and a calm two-column layout (evidence/desktop-form.png, desktop-rail.png), but the rail is denser than the form and at 390px the floating 'Prototype controls' bar covers the 'Your workspace at a glance' heading (mobile-overlap.png). A less dense mobile rail and non-overlapping demo chrome would raise this to 4.
rationale.interaction_completeness: Eight demo states are selectable (implementation/index.html:396-405); project-creation failure (implementation/app.js:352-365), partial invitation failure with retry (implementation/app.js:749+) and seat-limit disabling are implemented, not merely described.
rationale.accessibility_responsiveness: checks.json reports 2 controls without an accessible name in both viewports; fieldsets with legends, a progressbar meter and reduced-motion support are present (implementation/app.js:508-520). Naming every control and keeping the demo panel out of content flow would raise this.
rationale.implementation_quality: A 1,251-line IIFE with esc() on interpolated values, guarded localStorage (implementation/app.js:106-125) and view-scoped render functions; no dependencies or console errors.

rationale.product_understanding: analysis.md separates facts (lines 5-16), assumptions (18-26) and unknowns (28-37), and the role table keeps Admin outside billing/deletion without claiming settings rights (line 112).
rationale.ux_reasoning: Project-first ordering with a dynamic primary action - 'Continue without inviting' when empty, 'Send N invitations' when filled (implementation/app.js:402-429) - plus Save & exit and a paused-from resume (implementation/app.js:262-289). The optional invite step still sits before the 'project ready' screen, adding one surface before confirmation (implementation/app.js:984).
rationale.design_judgment: analysis.md §2 'Why project-first' (lines 83-91) and the risk/mitigation set (166-188) name alternatives and costs, including the height role cards add (line 169).
rationale.visual_hierarchy: desktop-form.png shows an editorial heading, one filled primary action and a quiet secondary exit; desktop-rail.png keeps progress and workspace facts subordinate, and mobile-form.png keeps the field and CTA within the first viewport.
rationale.interaction_completeness: Per-row sending, sent and failed states with retry and partial failure (implementation/app.js:451-511), an Owner/Admin/Member preview with a Member gate (implementation/app.js:1261-1274), seat cap and empty states are implemented.
rationale.accessibility_responsiveness: checks.json: one h1, zero controls without an accessible name, axe 0 violations on both viewports; skip link, aria-pressed segmented control, live regions and focus-to-heading are present (implementation/index.html:13,46-50). The only blemish is the 12.5px 'Save & exit' text link with no padding (implementation/styles.css:628-635), a sub-24px tap target on mobile.
rationale.implementation_quality: Event delegation (implementation/app.js:1361) with epoch guards on async work (implementation/app.js:342-348), escapeHtml on interpolated strings, guarded storage and a pagehide save (implementation/app.js:1455); a 73-line shell with rendered views keeps it maintainable.

critical_defects: The 'Save & exit' control is a 12.5px text link with zero padding (styles.css:628-635), below the 24px minimum target size on mobile.
strengths: Strong editorial hierarchy and a clean single-focus card on both viewports.
Dynamic primary action adapts to whether invitations have been entered.
Per-row invitation status, partial failure and retry are implemented with role preview gates.

comparison: Candidate B has the stronger first screen and the cleaner accessibility evidence (one h1, no unnamed controls, axe clean), while Candidate A matches it on product reasoning and ships a few more recovery states such as project-creation failure and a deep-link guard. Both keep the solo path unblocked; B edges ahead on visual hierarchy and verified accessible naming.
limitations: Only step-1 desktop and mobile screenshots were supplied, so later screens were judged from source and checks.json rather than visually. Touch-target sizes, screen-reader behaviour and real async delivery could not be measured; the floating prototype controls are demo chrome and may not reflect product UI.
